robust_themes.statement: The ₹1,199 'Special Deal Price' reads as suspicious without an anchor price; within-target buyers want to know what it was before the deal.
The 'Prime' badge reads as cosmetic premium signaling rather than a real tier or feature upgrade.
Closed case alone leaves the product visually unfelt; comprehension of what's new drops without buds-in-ear or case-open imagery.

fragile_themes.statement: The 'Shop Now' CTA places conversion pressure that feels mistimed for a deal-led claim — like the ad doesn't trust its own discount to do the work.

within_target_findings.statement: Within the value-conscious Boat-repeat buyer target, the ad gets attention via the price hook but loses comprehension immediately afterward — the price is doing all the work, and there's nothing else to anchor on.

The discount mechanic (₹1,199 'Special Deal Price' with no anchor) lands as cheap-feeling brand signaling rather than a real saving; the within-target voice is 'these were probably 800 last week and Boat just slapped Prime on the box'.

outside_target_findings.statement: Specialty audiophile dispositions read the ad as confirmation that Boat plays in a tier they have already exited; not damaging, but reinforces brand-extension headwinds.

commute_scroll.friction_summary: Price hook earns a pause; absence of a real product differentiator means the scroll resumes within a second or two.

pre_purchase_research.friction_summary: Active comparison-shoppers anchor on the deal price and open into Flipkart/Amazon to verify — the ad does its directional job, even if the trust gap remains.

late_night_wind_down.friction_summary: Low-attention scroll: product never registers, brand recall is the only takeaway, no purchase intent surfaces.

Prime sticker is doing more work than the product
I'd at least want to see them in someone's ear before I believe this is a real upgrade
